conventions.convention: ReLU networks permit skip edges, have affine outputs, and have depth H+2 where H is the maximum number of hidden units on a directed hidden path. Weights count connection coefficients and unit biases.

Activation means strictly positive preactivation; zero is inactive. Count only cells with nonempty ambient interior, and count distinct patterns separately even when their affine output formulas agree.

The Sobolev ball uses the maximum of the essential suprema of all weak derivatives through order n, including the function. AC is assumed, and lower derivatives use their Lipschitz representatives extended to the closed cube.
Continuous parameter selection means continuity for the uniform norm on the Sobolev ball; the decoder has no continuity or measurability requirement.
The rank-sensitive region bounds concern standard adjacent-layer networks, rather than the general skip-edge architecture.

In the semi-algebraic separation theorem, computational layers exclude inputs and include the output gate. Gates share one list of at most t predicate polynomials; decision-tree node budgets include leaves.

load_bearing.statement: For M>0 and 0<ε<M², a ReLU network approximates xy on [-M,M]² within ε, vanishes on both coordinate axes, and has depth, weights and computation units at most C_M(1+log(M²/ε)).
Under AC, the tensor-hat weighted Taylor sum for a member of the maximum-norm unit W^{n,∞} ball on (0,1)^d extends continuously to the closed cube and has L∞ error at most C(d,n)N^{-n}.

For each integer q≥0, the qth tent iterate maps each of 2^q dyadic intervals bijectively onto [0,1], with slope magnitude 2^q, and has a ReLU implementation with 2q hidden units, q hidden layers, O(q+1) weights and depth q+2.

For m polynomials of degree at most d in k variables, strict sign vectors and either binary threshold convention have at most (2md+1)^k realizations; ternary sign vectors have at most (4md+1)^k realizations. The bounds also hold on any restricted domain.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every integer m≥0 and every continuous map h:S^m→R^m, there exists x∈S^m with h(x)=h(-x).

A fixed scalar-output ReLU architecture with W≥1 counted coefficients and biases and depth at most L has fixed-threshold VC dimension at most CW² and at most CWL log(2W), for either strict or non-strict thresholding.

Set R_{L+1}(r)=1 and R_ℓ(r)=Σ_{j=0}^{min(r,n_ℓ)} binom(n_ℓ,j) R_{ℓ+1}(min(r,n_ℓ-j)). A current activation cell with affine image dimension at most r produces at most R_ℓ(r) activation cells through layers ℓ,…,L.

For every integer n≥3, a scalar-input adjacent-layer ReLU block of hidden width n has exactly n interior breakpoints on [0,1] and maps each resulting interval bijectively onto [0,1]. Composing widths n_1,…,n_L≥3 yields ∏(n_ℓ+1) full-dimensional activation regions.
For an L-Lipschitz real function on [0,1] and integer N≥1, its degree-N Bernstein polynomial has uniform error at most L/(2√N).

published_dependencies.used_for: Weak-derivative membership, maximum W^{n,∞} norm, and the Countable Choice convention.
Lipschitz representatives on convex cubes and intervals under AC; its gradient uses the Euclidean norm, giving the grid proof's √d bound.
Interior mollification convergence for finite p, used with p=1 rather than an unsupported W^{k,∞} density assertion.
Derivative identities for interior mollification through order n in the Taylor remainder argument.
Explicit choice assumptions in Sobolev and cohomological suppliers.
The choice convention inherited by the Sobolev and mollification interfaces.
AC implies the Countable Choice needed by the analysis suppliers.
Sphere notation, including S^0, in Borsuk–Ulam.
The polynomial mod-two cohomology ring and skeletal restriction isomorphisms used to exclude odd sphere maps.
Projective space as the antipodal quotient and a finite CW complex of the indicated dimension.
Vanishing of degree-m cohomology on RP^{m-1}, under AC.
Equality of pullbacks for the explicit projective-space homotopies.
Naturality of powers of the degree-one projective cohomology class.
Polynomial expansions and degree bookkeeping in the elementary sign-pattern proof.
Existence of maxima on nonempty closed bounded sets in the sign-pattern proof.
Vanishing gradients at interior polynomial maxima.
Shattering and VC dimension for the fixed-architecture lower-bound argument.
